provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Each rocket is one 8-connected group of non-background cells. Its head centre is the cell whose four orthogonal neighbours are all non-background; a centre in colour palette[4] is preferred. The tail cells are the palette[1] cells outside the plus. The flight direction runs from the mean position of the tail cells towards the centre, taking whichever axis has the larger offset. This works in visible coordinates for all four flight directions, so no normalisation is needed. The D4 transform only changes which way rockets point, and that is read from the pixels. The palette only changes the background, tail and hub colours, which are set as the constants palette[8], palette[1] and palette[4]. The shift is the distance from the leading arm to the grid border in the flight direction. All rockets are erased first, then redrawn shifted. Tail cells are translated, and the five plus cells are reflected through the centre (a 180-degree rotation) before translating. The arm colours (0,2,3,5,6,7,9 after palette mapping) never need to be identified.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain: rockets are separated by at least one background row or column, so they never merge under 8-connectivity, and each has a full plus with an interior centre. The constructor guarantees both: row bands are 4-5 apart and the grid is at least 7 wide. Rockets on opposite sides that share a band are not possible in this generator. If the tail mean were equidistant on both axes, the rocket is left unchanged; this cannot happen for well-formed rockets. The program has not been run on any fixtures. I checked the logic by hand against the constructor: the shift is width-6 (or height-6), which matches the arm-to-border distance, and the colour placement output[brow-r][...] is exactly a 180-degree reflection of the plus about the shifted centre. I found no constructor defects or contradictions between the fixtures and the rule.
